lines.text: Dum didicit uarios curſus, ac tempora Lunæ,
lines.en: While he learned the various courses and times of the Moon,

lines.text: Indè onus Atlantis ſubijt Tirynthius heros
lines.en: Thence the Tirynthian hero took up the burden of Atlas

lines.text: Ac tulit ardentem ſtellis lucentibus orbem,
lines.en: And bore the orb burning with shining stars,

lines.text: Edoctus cœli leges Chirone magiſtro.
lines.en: Taught the laws of heaven by the master Chiron.

lines.text: Nec minor Herculea fuit, indignusúe labor ui.
lines.en: Nor was the labor less than Herculean strength, or unworthy of it.

lines.text: Quid poterat maius tentare? atq; intima mundi,
lines.en: What greater thing could he attempt? and the innermost parts of the world,

lines.text: Aſtrigeræq́; domus penetralia cum duce tanto
lines.en: And the inner chambers of the star-bearing house with so great a leader

lines.text: Scandere, metiriq́; orbes ac ſidera cœli?
lines.en: To climb, and to measure the orbs and stars of heaven?

lines.text: Heroum uirtus hæc ſancta, ducumq́; potentum
lines.en: This holy virtue of heroes, and of powerful leaders

lines.text: Accendit ſtudium generoſæ poſteritatis.
lines.en: Kindles the zeal of noble posterity.

lines.text: Iſta ſuos mirata duces ad ſidera tollit,
lines.en: That [posterity], admiring its leaders, raises them to the stars,

lines.text: Æternamq́; tenêre inter flagrantia famam
lines.en: And commands them to hold eternal fame among the blazing

lines.text: Corpora ſtellarum iubet. Hinc eſt clarus Orion
lines.en: Bodies of the stars. Hence Orion is famous

lines.text: Sideribus, rapido iunctusq́; Hyperionis orbi
lines.en: In the stars, and joined to the rapid orb of Hyperion

lines.text: Centaurus, pulchrisq́; nitens Tirynthius aſtris,
lines.en: Is the Centaur, and the Tirynthian shining with beautiful stars,

lines.text: Cuius & immenſos, ſigna ad duodena labores
lines.en: Whose immense labors, at the twelve signs,

lines.text: Antiqui retulere chori. Sic notior Orphei
lines.en: The ancient choruses recounted. Thus the lyre of Orpheus

lines.text: Eſt lyra, diuino quæ uaſtas carmine ſyluas,
lines.en: Is better known, which by its divine song moved the vast woods,

lines.text: Æquora, ſaxa, feras, homines commouit & ipſos
lines.en: The seas, the rocks, the wild beasts, and men themselves,

lines.text: Sæpe Deos, reſonansq́; poli ſecreta, uiasq́;
lines.en: And often the Gods, and resounding the secrets of the pole, and the ways,

lines.text: Emeruit rutilas inter non infima ſtellas
lines.en: It earned a place not the lowest among the glowing stars

lines.text: Nomina, quæ poterit non ulla abolêre uetuſtas.
lines.en: Names, which no antiquity will be able to abolish.

lines.text: Hæc pia poſteritas dabit immortalibus illis
lines.en: This pious posterity will give to those immortals

lines.text: Heroum meritis decora immortalia, donec
lines.en: Immortal honors for the merits of heroes, until

lines.text: Sublapſo magnus ſub cardine corruet orbis.
lines.en: The great orb shall collapse under the fallen hinge.

lines.text: Spontè hic nobilium Nili prope flumina regum,
lines.en: Here of its own accord, near the rivers of the Nile, of noble kings,

lines.text: Nomina prætereo uix enumeranda, nec iſtis
lines.en: I pass over names scarcely to be enumerated, nor to those

lines.text: Verſibus apta, & quos Romanaq́; Graiaq́; tellus,
lines.en: Verses suited, and those whom the Roman and Greek earth,

summary.headline: Preface on Heroes Among the Stars
summary.text: Poetic preface praises Chiron’s teaching of celestial laws, Hercules bearing Atlas, Orion, the Centaur, and Orpheus, whose heroic deeds and constellations preserve immortal fame among the stars; it then turns toward ancient kings and peoples by the Nile, in Roman and Greek lands.
